title: Three reports from the server inventory

ticket.subject: Ops review: down servers and the busiest ones
body: This morning's inventory export is in `inventory/servers.csv` (Name, Region, Status, CpuPct). For the ops
review I need three files in `reports/`:
1. `reports/down.csv`: the servers whose Status is `down`, with the columns `Name,Region` only, sorted by Name.
2. `reports/down-by-region.csv`: one row per region that has down servers, with the columns `Region,Down`
3. `reports/busiest.txt`: the names of the three servers with the highest CpuPct, highest first, one per line.
Plain CSV: a header line and the rows, no `#TYPE` line. PowerShell is the natural tool here (objects in, objects
out); bash with awk and sort works too.

acceptance.text: reports/down.csv lists the down servers (Name, Region), sorted by Name.
reports/down-by-region.csv counts the down servers per region (Region, Down).
reports/busiest.txt names the three busiest servers, highest CpuPct first.

hints: `Import-Csv inventory/servers.csv` gives objects with properties. Pipe them: `Where-Object Status -eq 'down' | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object Name, Region | Export-Csv reports/down.csv -NoTypeInformation`.
`Group-Object Region` counts for you, in properties called Name and Count. A calculated property renames them: `Select-Object @{n='Region'; e={$_.Name}}, @{n='Down'; e={$_.Count}}`.

Import-Csv reads every value as text, so `Sort-Object CpuPct` puts "9" above "85". Sort on the number: `Sort-Object { [int]$_.CpuPct } -Descending`, then `Select-Object -First 3 -ExpandProperty Name`.
Windows PowerShell 5.1's `Export-Csv` adds a `#TYPE` line unless you pass `-NoTypeInformation`; its `>` writes UTF-16 (the checker reads it, other tools may not).
